'''Elguja "Gia" Gvazava''' ({{lang-ka|ელგუჯა [გია] გვაზავა}}) (born February 22, 1952) is a [[Georgia (country)|Georgian]] politician. Being a native of Georgia's [[autonomous republic]] of [[Abkhazia]] and a member of the local legislature since 1991, Gvazava was forced, along with most of the region's [[Ethnic cleansing of Georgians in Abkhazia|Georgian population]], to flee the [[War in Abkhazia (1992–1993)|secessionist victory]] in Abkhazia in 1993. From March 20, 2009, to April 8, 2019, he served a chairman of the Supreme Council of Abkhazia, based [[Government of the Autonomous Republic of Abkhazia|in exile]] in the Georgian capital of [[Tbilisi]].<ref name="scara">Supreme Council of Abkhazia, Georgia. Biography of Elguja Gvazava. ([http://scara.gov.ge/ka/home/53-biografia.html URL]). Accessed 2011-04-15. ([https://web.archive.org/web/20110826190212/http://scara.gov.ge/ka/home/53-biografia.html Archived] by [[WebCite]]®)</ref><ref name="civ080419">{{cite news |title=Abkhazian Supreme Council-in-Exile Elects New Chairman |url=https://civil.ge/archives/301426 |accessdate=8 April 2019 |work=Civil Georgia |date=8 April 2019 |ref=301426}}</ref>

==Career==
Born in [[Ochamchire]], [[Abkhaz ASSR]], [[Georgian SSR]], Gvazava graduated from the [[Abkhazian State University|Sukhumi Pedagogical Institute]] with a degree in biology in 1974 and continued his postgraduate training at the Institute of Medical Genetics in [[Moscow]] from 1976 to 1981. In 1982, he acquired a position of [[docent]] at the Sukhumi State University and, in 1991, he was elected to the Supreme Council of Abkhazia, a local legislature. Gvazava retained both his academic and legislative positions when the Georgian factions of both university and the Supreme Council were forced to relocate to Tbilisi in the aftermath of the 1992—93 war in Abkhazia. In 1995, he was further elected Deputy Chairman of the Supreme Council of Abkhazia-in-exile.<ref name="scara"/> Simultaneously, from 1992 to 2004, he was a member of the [[Parliament of Georgia]].<ref>[http://www.parliament.ge/pages/archive_en/parl99/gvazava_elguja_e.htm Gvazava Elguja]. Parliament of Georgia. 2003-07-23. Accessed 2011-04-15</ref> On March 20, 2009, he became a chairman of the Supreme Council of Abkhazia.<ref>[http://en.trend.az/news/politics/foreign/1443774.html New chairman elected for Supreme Council of Abkhazia]. [[Trend News Agency]]. 2009-03-20. Accessed 2011-04-15</ref> He was re-elected on April 7, 2014<ref>[http://abkhazeti.info/abkhazia/2014/1396904114.php Internet version of Abkhaz newspaper Наша Абхазия]</ref> On April 8, 2019, he was succeeded by [[Jemal Gamakharia]].<ref name="civ080419"/>
